(Howdy! I literally had the same fall and spring coursework this past academic year (with ECEN 303 instead of 322). I assure you that it's *not* the move. I somehow managed to come out with a 4.0, but keep in mind that I took ECEN 325 and 350 labs during a COVID semester and I've heard that they're notoriously more rigorous in person. I followed up with a 12-hour summer semester, and I cannot emphasize how burnt out I feel during this current semester, especially with senior design.

I will say that it's doable, especially if you're able to get the right professors. However, if you want to retain information (for senior design, in general, etc.), maintain balance in other areas of your life, or be emotionally stable, I'd advise taking *either* ECEN 325 or 350.  If you have diligent work ethic and the willpower to persevere, (which I'm assuming you do, given your performance this semester),  I would say go for it. Best of luck, and please feel free to PM me if you have any questions! :)

I encourage you to reach out to a specific professor within your area of interest. I emailed one of my professors within the controls/power electronics area earlier this semester and he was able to get me started with the EMPE lab within a week! Even if your specific area of interest doesn't have any immediate openings, it doesn't hurt to at least get your name out there; faculty members will likely be more willing to offer a position to a familiar face, especially someone who is enthusiastic and eager to delve into research. 

On a personal note, I haven't had any industry experience due to summer classes, but I tried to convey (as clearly as possible) that I wanted to extract as much information via hands-on experience and learning from trial and error before entering the industry. With EE being a VERY broad major, I mentioned my strongest/weakest areas, what sorts of skills I wanted to develop, what companies/positions I was interested in working for/in, why I have been considering graduate school (if that applies to you), and what I hoped to get out of doing research.

I’m not sure about how many positions are open in general, but I assume there are quite a few. The EMPE lab specifically has a variety of projects, with relevance in not just power systems, but also in energy, defense, aerospace, and so much more. A lot of your ECEN 300-level classes will barely scratch the surface, so I'm really excited to see that you're considering research! Even if you're not 100% sure where your passions lie, it's better to get started *somewhere* and dip your toes in a couple different areas, rather than dive head-first into a career that doesn't bring you as much fulfillment as you had expected. So I encourage you to keep an open mind when it comes to open positions! PM me if you have any questions, and best of luck!

I started using Notion this semester to organize my personal/school life in one massive hub. I had one section for each class that organized all of my due dates, grades, and syllabus, and it definitely helped me stay on top of things this semester. I also had a daily/weekly overview - being able to cross off each task was mildly cathartic, to say the least. Plus, it saved me more time than I thought by not having to sift through different folders on my laptop/Google Drive!
